Block schematics · rev 2 · 11 Oct 2026

ZU67DR Pulse Array

Four modules, each a HamGeek XCZU67DR card plugged into a custom AFE + PA carrier. Together they drive 32 RF-DAC columns and 32 one-bit rows. A shared reference and SYSREF keep them in step, and a PC controls everything over Ethernet.

Concept

Overview: how the signal gets to the DUT

Patterns go from the PC into each RFSoC card. The card generates the outputs in two ways: an RF-DAC for arbitrary waveforms and a GTY serializer for fast one-bit pulses. The carrier board amplifies both to 3 V, sets each channel's DC level, and drives the DUT. One clock source keeps all four modules on the same clock. Every module is built the same, so the sync option is a cable-selected profile (rear cables plus a software profile): a sync unit, any module as root through a passive splitter, or a daisy chain. A small PC, a Minisforum MS-A2 on the Ethernet switch, runs the system.

Concept

System: four modules, one clock source, one PC

Every module gets the clock and the trigger from one source. All modules are built the same, so the sync options are cable-selected profiles: a sync unit, any module as root through a passive splitter, or a daisy chain, each a set of rear cables plus a software profile. The SYSREF is derived (each card makes its own from the shared 5 MHz CLK, the default) or true (the same 5 MHz edge on each card's SYNC pin, same cables). The control PC, a Minisforum MS-A2 on the Ethernet switch, only uploads patterns, sets DC levels and reads back status.

The clock source box follows the sync profile chosen in the Configuration panel or in Daisy-chain option: sync unit, Master + splitter, Master + 2 splitters (legacy cabling) or daisy chain; one module is the bench profile with no sync cables. The choice carries through power, cable count, rack height and the 3D model; Sync & timing has the profile table.

Hardware

One module: HamGeek card + carrier

On the left is the HamGeek card as delivered, read from XCZU67DR_PCIE_V1.pdf. Amber blocks need a rework or limit the design. On the right is the carrier we design. It takes the eight GTY lanes through a PCIe x8 slot and the eight DAC outputs through SSMC jumpers, then adds the front ends, DC levels, power and a clock zone that software switches between the sync options. Every card gets the same one-time prep, so all modules are built alike. Each amber block has a row in Card findings.

Four design rules carry over to layout: put the eight one-bit (GTY) strips nearest the PCIe slot so the 20 Gb/s lanes stay short, and the eight RF-DAC strips beyond them, since their signals arrive by SSMC jumpers anyway; route all eight one-bit lanes as length-matched 100 Ω pairs; keep each output channel as a strip that runs straight to its front-panel SMA; and give the DC-level buffers their own ground return so DC current stays out of the RF ground under the amplifiers.

Pulse fidelity: lowest frequency and edge speed

Which parts set the lowest frequency and the edge speed, and what does a 500 ps, 3 V pulse look like after the chain? Every coupling capacitor, balun and bias choke adds a high-pass corner. The source edge, the amplifier and the balun set the high end.

What the low corner does to a pulse

A high-pass corner fL makes the top of a pulse sag. Over a pulse of width τ the top drops by 1 − exp(−2π fL τ). For 500 ps even a 1 MHz corner costs only 0.3 %, so short pulses pass AC coupling well. The low corner matters for long pulses, slow DC-level steps and long patterns.

After AC coupling, a unipolar pulse train settles so that its average is zero. The baseline moves down by duty × amplitude: 500 ps every 100 ns at 3 V gives 15 mV. Corners well below 1 / period keep this shift. Corners near or above it let the baseline recover between pulses.

What sets the edge

The 10–90 % rise time is about 0.35 / bandwidth. The GTY edge (about 20 ps), the RF-DAC (about 60 ps), the amplifier and the balun each limit the bandwidth. Their rise times add roughly as root-sum-square.

The carrier parts are on the Carrier schematic: T1, L1/L2/L5 and C1–C4 on the one-bit outputs, C11 and L10–L12 on the DAC outputs. The card's own DAC path is in Card findings.

Formulas used here

  • Capacitor into 50 Ω: f = 1 / (2π · 50 Ω · C). Choke across 25 Ω: f = 25 Ω / (2π L).
  • Droop over a pulse of width τ: 1 − exp(−2π fL τ). For several corners, use the sum of the corners.
  • Cascade −3 dB: solve |H(f)|² = ½ with |H|² = Π f² / (f² + fi²) for the high-pass corners and Π 1 / (1 + (f / fi)²) for the low-pass limits.
  • Rise time 10–90 % ≈ 0.35 / BW. Parts combine roughly as root-sum-square.
  • Baseline shift after AC coupling = duty × amplitude (0.5 % × 3 V = 15 mV).
  • P1dB for a Vpeak pulse into 50 Ω: 10·log10(V² / (2 · 50 Ω) / 1 mW). 3 V needs 19.5 dBm, 4 V needs 22 dBm.

Pulse fidelity lab

The carrier uses staged chokes: 4 µH + 100 µH + 1 mH ≈ 1.1 mH. Alone, 4 µH gives ≈ 1 MHz and 133 µH ≈ 30 kHz across 25 Ω.

Step 5

Sync and timing

All modules have to start their patterns on the same clock edge. The trigger only arms each module; the start is the next SYSREF edge. Only one 5 MHz clock is shared between modules. With the derived SYSREF (the default) each card makes its own SYSREF from that clock, locked to the shared edge; with the true SYSREF the card takes the shared 5 MHz edge itself on its SYNC pin. Either way every module has the same edge, so the trigger can arrive anywhere inside a 200 ns window and every module still starts on the same cycle.

Trigger alignment

TRIG reaches each module a few ns apart because cables and receivers differ. With SYSREF gating the trigger only arms the module and all modules start on the next SYSREF edge. Starting straight on TRIG copies the arrival spread into the outputs, rounded to the 4 ns fabric clock (250 MHz from the MMCM).

One build, every sync option

Every card and every carrier is built the same way. A sync option is a set of rear cables plus a software profile. Nothing is soldered, strapped or moved inside the box afterwards, and any module can be the root.

Card prep, once per card

  • SYSREF mod: remove R345 and R699, run a fixed-length coax from the J35 side of R345 to the LMK SYNC pin; fit an SMA on J35.
  • J67 soldered on 2-3 (J66 → CLKin0). Remove R340, so card U48 (the 10 MHz TCXO) stays off.
  • MIO26 (K19) set as an input. CLKin_SEL pins and the SPI readback (MIO33, 34, 36) open-drain only, because the LMK runs at 3.3 V and the PS bank at 1.8 V.
  • GTY TX4–7 coupling-cap rework, then an acceptance test (continuity, one BENCH-DZ lock, 5 MTS power cycles, one BENCH-TS sync).

Details and checklist: Card findings.

Carrier clock zone, the same on every carrier

  • U20, U22 and U28 are LMK00804B buffers with an LVCMOS input and a differential input (U22 VDDO 2.5 V from U60). U20 feeds card J66, U22 drives card J35, U28 drives J29.
  • Y1 (10 MHz TCXO with OE) and U29 (÷ 2) make LOCAL5, the 5 MHz root. Only the root turns them on.
  • U30 (TCA9538, I²C 0x70) sets every source. U61 passes the SYNC pin only when U30 P3 and J31 IO3 are both high. U59 holds U20, U22 and U30 off while the card is off.
  • J26 and J27 inputs: −3 dB tap, AC-coupled, idle low. They take square sources of 0.35–1.8 Vpp at 5 or 10 MHz. U27 runs in differential input mode.
  • Removed: U21 with its VCXO, JP1, JP3, J40, J41, J43, K1 and the Ethernet option E2.

What changes between options: only these cables

  • The rear cables on J26, J27, J28 and J29, and the external splitter(s) and TRIG star.
  • The profile each module gets from the PC: root flag, U30 settings, DZ or TS5, TRIG drive or listen.
  • Inside the box nothing moves: W21, W22, W23 and W25 are fixed in every profile.
  • After any re-cable, relock or profile change: re-sync the cards and re-run MTS (PG269 p.163, p.185–186).

Risks and checks, in bench order

  1. Vivado: RFdc IP with a 125 MHz PL clock against the 625 MHz AXI4-Stream clock under MTS.
  2. LMK00804B input network at 0.25–1.3 Vpp, 5 and 10 MHz, idle low with nothing connected.
  3. BENCH-DZ phase repeatability over 20+ power cycles.
  4. TS5: exactly one gated edge per sync (MON_SYNC count = 1).
  5. PLL1 loop at a 5 MHz PFD in PLLatinum; any filter change goes into the card prep.
  6. Splitter edge rate and port-to-port delay match; TRIG level budget at the chosen N.
  7. Then the first multi-module MASTER-DZ.

Tracked in Roadmap & open items.

The clock tree below shows the sync-unit star (UNIT-TS), which carries every signal on its own cable. In the other profiles the root is Y1 + U29 on one module's carrier, or a lab generator, and the same carrier inputs take it; see Distribution options below.

Card J32 (SYS_CLK_OUT): the GTY reference

J32 is the vertical SMA on the card's top edge (schematic page 18), and the card's only external clock output.

  • Source. LMK04828 SDCLKOUT5. It shares its clock group with DCLKOUT4 (ADC_REFCLK1, an RF-ADC tile we do not use), so J32 is free. It can be a device clock, VCO ÷ 1 to 32 (≥ 93.75 MHz at VCO1 = 3000 MHz; 250 MHz = ÷ 12), or the SYSREF divider output, VCO ÷ 8 to 8191 (5 MHz = ÷ 600).
  • Electrical. Single-ended, DC-coupled LVPECL: P side through R651 33 Ω with a 240 Ω emitter pull-down (R338), N side to GND through C395 0.1 µF. About 0.4–0.6 Vpp into 50 Ω (estimate), more in the LVPECL 2000 mV format. Needs an inline DC block.
  • Card plan at VCO1 = 3000 MHz: DAC_REFCLK 500 MHz = ÷ 6, SYSREF 5 MHz = ÷ 600, PL_CLK 125 MHz = ÷ 24. One MMCM makes 625 MHz (× 5) for the DAC AXI4-Stream (10 GS/s, DUC bypass, 16 samples per word) and 250 MHz (× 2) for the fabric and the GTY user clock. Under MTS the AXI clocks come from PL_CLK through the MMCM, never from clk_dacX (PG269 p.188, p.190, p.224, p.359). A 250 MHz PL_CLK fails, because 625 / 250 = 2.5 is not an integer. Vivado check; fallbacks: VCO0 2500 MHz with PL_CLK 625 MHz, or 8 GS/s with 500 MHz.

Yes, as the GTY reference, in every carrier profile

J32 at 250 MHz → short coax W23 → carrier J45 "GTY REF IN" → C20 DC block → U27 (LMK1D1204) → PCIE_CLK edge pins (10 nF series on the card) → GTY quad A refclk1, shared with quad B. QPLL0 N = 40 → VCO 10 GHz → 20 Gb/s full rate. U27 runs in differential input mode (IN0_P with 49.9 Ω, IN0_N AC-coupled to VAC_REF0): its single-ended LVCMOS mode needs ≥ 0.4 Vpp and stops at 250 MHz, our rate.

The GTY clock is then locked and phase-fixed to the card's own PL_CLK, DAC and SYSREF clocks: 250 MHz = 50 × 5 MHz has one fixed phase to SYSREF. W23 never moves in any profile.

Start-up rule. The card LMK locks, syncs and settles before the GTY QPLL is released.

As a chain clock: only for bare cards

Card-only chain A1. J32 in SYSREF-divider mode (5 MHz, LVPECL 2000 mV) → DC block → next card J66, derived SYSREF, no carriers. The GTY then runs from the card's free-running SI5341 (one-bit rows not locked to the DACs). Each card's SPI sync briefly stops its J32, so the cards sync strictly root → tail. Bring-up only; see the Daisy-chain option.

No carrier profile takes SYSREF from card J32. The legacy two-splitter cabling now feeds both splitters from the root's J29.

Start-up sequence

  1. The PC sends each module its profile. The PS writes U30 over I²C (enable off, change the source, enable on), so no runt pulse reaches a card. Exactly one root: Y1 and LOCAL5 on one module, or the sync unit, or a lab generator.
  2. Every U20 passes CLK (J26, or LOCAL5 on a bench module) to card J66. U28 sends J29: LOCAL5 on the root, a relay of J26 in a chain, off on leaves and on the tail. U22 holds the card SYNC pin low.
  3. Each card LMK04828 locks PLL1 to CLK on J66 (CLKin0, MOS mode with LOS) and PLL2 to its VCXO. The PS reads RB_PLL1_LD and RB_PLL2_LD over SPI.
  4. Divider sync. DZ: SPI sync (SYNC_POL) in dual-loop with the pin held low, then switch to nested zero-delay with the SYSREF divider as feedback. TS5: lock straight into nested zero-delay with DCLKout8 feedback (UG1437 p.10); U61 then passes exactly one 5 MHz edge to the SYNC pin, timed by the FPGA from MON_CLK. Then wait a fixed settle time (≥ 10 loop time constants, from PLLatinum), not lock detect alone.
  5. Release the MMCMs (PL_CLK 125 MHz → 625 MHz DAC AXI, 250 MHz fabric), then the GTY QPLL0: card J32 250 MHz → W23 → J45 → U27 → PCIE_CLK, N = 40.
  6. Each card runs RF-DAC MTS with target −1 and reports its latency (PG269 p.186).
  7. The PC sets one common target: the largest latency seen over ≥ 5 power cycles plus 16 samples. MTS runs again and must return XRFDC_MTS_OK; the PC compares it with the value stored for this profile and cable set.
  8. GTY lanes come up with TX buffer bypass and phase alignment; the PL loads the patterns and applies the stored skew table.
  9. TRIG: the TRIG master (the sync unit re-timer, or one FPGA on J28 → card J64 → pin A10) zeroes a common 5 MHz period counter. Every module arms on a level-qualified TRIG and starts on the same SYSREF edge.

After any re-cable, relock, profile change or RF-DAC Reset Count change: stop, re-sync from step 2 and re-run MTS (PG269 p.163, p.185–186). In multi-module profiles the card LMK runs zero-delay; dual-loop is used only for a moment during the DZ divider sync, because it can lock at 4 or more VCO-grid positions ≈ 83 ps apart.

Pick a step to see the blocks it uses.

Splitter box and input levels (estimate)

A J29 output is 3.3 V behind 50 Ω: 1.65 Vpp into 50 Ω. A transformer splitter loses about 10·log10(N) + 1 dB, and the J26/J27 network taps −3 dB in front of the LMK00804B.

FeedSplitterAt the LMK00804B
Chain hop, sync unit or generatornone1.17 Vpp
Master star, 2 modules1:20.78 Vpp
Master star, 4 modulesZFSC-4-10.52 Vpp
Master star, 8 modulesZSC-2-1+ → 2 × ZFSC-4-1≈ 0.37 Vpp
Legacy two-splitter cabling1:2 + 1:8≈ 0.25 Vpp, measure

All of these sit inside the 0.25–1.3 Vpp input spec after the tap (LMK00804B VID 0.15–1.3 V, check); the legacy 1:2 + 1:8 path sits at its lower edge, so measure it. The highest high level, 2.24 V, stays under the 2.45 V common-mode maximum. U20 restores full swing, so card J66 sees ≈ 1.65 Vpp with fast edges.

Splitter band: ≤ 1 MHz to ≥ 500 MHz, so the 5 MHz square keeps sub-ns edges. ZFSC-4-1 (1–1000 MHz) for N ≤ 4; for N = 8 a ZSC-2-1+ feeding two ZFSC-4-1, or a wide-band 8-way (check). Not ZFSC-8-1 (0.5–175 MHz, slows the edges) and not ZFSC-2-1 (5–500 MHz, 5 MHz at the band edge). Square sources only, ≥ 0.2 V/ns at the connector; terminate unused ports in 50 Ω and use one cable length to every input, the loop-back included. AC-coupled transport is fine for the continuous SYSREF of MTS (PG269 p.187), not for a pulsed DC-coupled SYSREF.

Distribution options

Every option runs the same carrier and the same card prep: the build differences are none. They differ in where CLK, SYSREF and TRIG come from, which cables are plugged and which profile is loaded. For 2 to 8 modules in one rack, Master + splitter with derived SYSREF (MASTER-DZ) is the recommended option: one passive splitter and no box. MASTER-TS runs on the same cables when a true SYSREF is wanted.

Card J57 and J64: can we use them?

Both are SSMC jacks in the card's front-edge column (schematic page 17). J64 reaches the rear TRIG IO over a fixed internal coax. J57 has no rear port: it is reached through the front SSMC access. Neither needs a board change.

J64 PPS_IN: yes, as TRIG IO

J64 → R245 33 Ω series → FPGA pin A10 (3.3 V HD bank), with R248 1 kΩ to ground and a TPD4E001 ESD diode. It is a direct FPGA I/O, so the FPGA sets the direction.

  • As input: a direct trigger into the PL, LVCMOS33 threshold, 1 kΩ load. The source should be series-terminated.
  • As output: the FPGA driver plus 33 Ω is close to a 50 Ω series-terminated source into coax.
  • No tweak. Do not add a 50 Ω shunt: it would load the driver.

The rear TRIG IO SMA (J28) is cabled straight to card J64: one internal coax, W25, ≈ 480 mm as routed at the 235 mm card (≈ 400–560 mm for 160–320 mm cards, estimate). The TRIG master drives, the others listen. J65 IO3 now carries SYNC_GATE.

Level budget at A10 (VIH 2.0 V): a resistive star keeps ≈ 2.4 V at 4 modules (estimate), but only ≈ 1.9–2.2 V at 8, and the 480 mm W25 stubs ring. So N ≤ 4: resistive star or a short bus; N > 4: an active TRIG fan-out in the kit (≈ $30–60, estimate) or the GNSS-armed start. Listeners arm only on 4 consecutive high samples of the 250 MHz fabric clock, so a reflection cannot arm twice. TRIG only has to land inside one 200 ns SYSREF period.

J57 GNSS: yes, for time and arming, not as a clock

J57 → NEO-M8N RF_IN, with antenna bias from VCC_RF through L40 10 nH, so it takes an active antenna. The receiver's TIMEPULSE goes only to FPGA pin A9 (GNSS_PPS), not to the LMK. GNSS gives time of day and a PPS of tens-of-ns class (NEO-M8N timepulse accuracy: check the datasheet). That is not a reference for ps alignment.

  • Antenna feed: there is no rear GNSS port. The antenna (or a GNSS splitter arm) goes to card J57 SSMC through the front SSMC access (inlet plate off) or a front-panel feed-through fitted by the user. The card supplies the antenna bias; nothing on the card changes.
  • Time stamps: absolute time on every run.
  • GNSS-armed start: every module arms on the same GNSS second and starts on the first common SYSREF edge after it. The PPS spread (tens of ns) is far below the 200 ns SYSREF period, so no TRIG cable is needed when all modules see GNSS: one active antenna and a GNSS splitter with DC pass on one port to every card J57, or one antenna per module. The modules still share CLK. If a PPS lands within ≈ 50 ns of a SYSREF edge on any module, the PC moves to the next second.
  • Set-ups far apart: common time without a cable between them.

Calibration measures the fixed cable, trace and MTS delays once and trims them with sample shifts, bit shifts, the TX phase interpolator and, below 100 ps, clock phase (DAC_REFCLK ADLY if the bench allows it), cable length or waveform shaping. The after-calibration figures keep 10 % of those three terms and leave part-to-part and drift at full size. The checks use the worst case.

Daisy-chain option

The sync unit is not the only way to share a clock. Any module can be the root: its Y1 TCXO and U29 make the 5 MHz, and the others take it through a passive splitter or along a chain of short cables. Every carrier is the same board; root, relay, leaf and tail are settings in the software profile, not straps.

Master + splitter · recommended

One external splitter. The root's J29 sends 5 MHz into a passive 1:N splitter that feeds every CLK IN, its own included. TRIG IO goes through a resistive star. MASTER-DZ (derived SYSREF) by default; MASTER-TS on the same cables.

Master + 2 splitters · legacy

The old cabling, still supported. The root's J29 feeds a 1:2 splitter, then splitter A to every CLK IN and splitter B to every SYSREF IN. True SYSREF, but it adds nothing over MASTER-TS.

Daisy chain

Hop by hop. J29 of one module feeds CLK IN of the next; TRIG IO runs as a short bus. CHAIN-DZ or CHAIN-TS on the same cables. Fewest cables, but delay and drift add up per hop.

Sync unit (star)

A separate 1U box sends CLK, SYSREF and TRIG to every module over phase-matched cables (UNIT-TS, or UNIT-DZ without SYSREF). It is described in Sync & timing.

One clock does both jobs

The chain and the one-splitter star carry a single 5 MHz clock, the SYSREF rate. In DZ each module locks its card LMK04828 to it in nested zero-delay mode, with the SYSREF divider as the feedback. The divider then has one fixed phase to the incoming edge, so every module makes its own SYSREF. No SYSREF cable runs between modules, and no module samples another module's SYSREF. In TS5 the same edge also reaches the card SYNC pin once, through U22 and the U61 gate, and the card runs zero-delay with DCLKout8 feedback (UG1437 p.10).

Modules are numbered from the root: module k sits k hops after module 0. The GTY reference does not ride on the chain: each card loops its own J32 (250 MHz, one phase to the 5 MHz edge) back through carrier J45, in every profile. Only the card-only chain uses J32 for the chain clock. This stage uses 5 MHz to match Sync & timing.

Recommendation

  • Use the derived SYSREF (DZ) unless a true SYSREF is needed. It removes the SYSREF cable, every sampling window between modules and the LMK04832 output limit. TS5 runs on the same cables as a cross-check.
  • 2 to 8 modules in one rack: Master + splitter (MASTER-DZ). No box, 1U and about 10 W saved, one passive splitter and a resistive TRIG star (active fan-out above 4 modules), 2N + 1 timing cables (2N at N = 2). Every module sits one cable from the root, so no drift builds up.
  • True SYSREF wanted: MASTER-TS, or the sync unit (UNIT-TS). Every card already has the SYSREF mod, so both need only a different profile; the sync unit also needs its own cables.
  • 2 to 4 modules side by side: the chain (CHAIN-DZ) is the alternative with the fewest cables. With 8 modules seven hops drift about 52 ps at ΔT = 5 °C with α = 1.5 ps/°C per hop (to measure), so use a star.
  • Card-only chain A1: for bring-up of bare cards. It uses up J32, so the GTY runs from the card’s free-running SI5341 (one-bit rows not locked to the DACs).
  • Every carrier is identical. The clock zone (U20, U22 and U28 LMK00804B, Y1 + U29, U30, U59, U60, U61) makes any module root, relay, leaf or tail by software. U21, JP1, JP3, J40, J41, J43, K1 and E2 are gone.

Corrections this study found

  1. As built, J66 goes through jumper J67 (pin 3) to CLKin0, and J35 goes through R345 to CLKin1. A separate SYSREF would have to use CLKin0 and push CLK onto J35, which shows no connector on the vendor photos.
  2. With the R699 wire mod (remove R345 and R699, wire J35 to the LMK SYNC pin with a fixed-length coax) J35 becomes a SYNC input. CLK then goes into J66 with J67 soldered on 2-3: carrier J32 → card J66, carrier J33 → card J35. The mod is now part of every card's prep.
  3. After the mod the SYNC pin is driven only from J35. In DZ profiles carrier U22 holds it low, because a floating or glitching pin resets the dividers after MTS (PG269 p.185). In TS5 exactly one gated edge passes.
  4. K19, which drove SYNC as built, is PS_MIO26: a PS GPIO, so the stock SYNC was software-timed only. The mod gives up nothing PL-timed; MIO26 is set as an input.
  5. J66 has a 49.9 Ω DC shunt (R344), so a carrier output into it needs a series 0.1 µF. LMK1D parts have LVDS outputs only: one LVDS leg into R344 gives ≈ 0.18 Vpp, below the 0.25 Vpp CLKin minimum. So U20 and U22 are LMK00804B with LVCMOS outputs (≈ 1.65 Vpp at J66).
  6. Card J32 is a DC-coupled LVPECL output (SDCLKOUT5), so a J32 → J66 link needs an inline SMA DC block. J32 is the card's only clock output: in the card-only chain it runs the SYSREF divider at 5 MHz and can no longer be the GTY reference.
  7. CLK must be a square wave: CLKin needs at least 0.15 V/ns (aim for 0.5 V/ns), and a 1 Vpp 10 MHz sine gives only 0.031 V/ns. J26 takes square sources only (0.35–1.8 Vpp, ≥ 0.2 V/ns at the connector); a sine lab reference goes through the kit function generator.
  8. In dual-loop the card LMK can lock at 4 or more VCO-grid positions ≈ 83 ps apart against CLK. Every multi-module profile therefore runs nested zero-delay; dual-loop is used only for a moment during the DZ divider sync.

The Card findings stage carries these corrections and the card-prep checklist.

Chain simulator

The model follows one SYSREF edge down the chain. It adds the cable and buffer delay per hop, places each module's SYSREF capture inside a 4 ns PL clock period, and adds up drift, jitter and the TRIG lead. Mismatch between buffers comes from a fixed seed, so the same settings always give the same result. The 4 ns window is the conservative case: with PL_CLK at 125 MHz (Vivado check) the capture window is 8 ns. The buffered lane models SYSREF sent down the chain through plain buffers, for comparison only.

What builds up along a chain

Delay and drift. Each hop adds a buffer and a cable, about 3 ns: 1.44 ns of 300 mm coax plus one LMK00804B (U28), 1–2.2 ns (check; the simulator uses 1.5 ns). With eight modules the last one runs about 21 ns behind the root. That delay is fixed, so calibration removes it with a start offset in 4 ns steps plus a fine trim. Drift is different. Every buffer in the path drifts with temperature, and the last module sees the sum: k·α·ΔT, 22.5 ps at four modules and 52.5 ps at eight. The MON_CLK edge monitor tracks it in service.

Jitter does not build up. Each buffer adds a few tens of fs at fast edges. The PLL1 loop of the next card LMK04828 filters it out. Every module's output jitter is set by its own LMK04828 and DAC PLL, about 100 fs, whether it sits first or eighth.

Trigger. The trigger only has to land inside one 200 ns SYSREF period. The root drives its TRIG IO 100 ns after a SYSREF edge. On the passive TRIG IO bus (N ≤ 4) the trigger sees only cable delay; the simulator still counts one buffer per hop, the conservative case. Either way it stays near the middle of the window on every module, at 100 ns ± 5 ns. Above 4 modules use the active fan-out or the GNSS-armed start.

True SYSREF on a chain (CHAIN-TS). The chain cables carry a true SYSREF too: each card samples the relayed 5 MHz edge once, on its own zero-delay VCO grid, so sampling points do not add up. With a ±60 ps guard about 36 % of modules land near an edge; the DCLKout8 half step (167 ps, check) moves them clear.

Failure. A chain depends on every module before it. U28 runs on the always-on U58 rail, so a module whose card is off still relays. A module with its 12 V off breaks the chain (there is no bypass relay), so re-cable around it.

Card only (A1). The HamGeek card can chain on its own: J32 of one card, in SYSREF-divider mode at 5 MHz, into J66 of the next through a DC block. The root card runs PLL1 on a 5 MHz PL clock (CLKin2) or in holdover. Each card's SPI sync briefly stops its J32, so the cards sync strictly root → tail, card k only after card k − 1 has settled: bring-up takes about N × the PLL1 settle time. The GTY then runs from the card’s free-running SI5341 (one-bit rows not locked to the DACs).

Which one. Master + splitter (MASTER-DZ) is the recommended option: no box, one passive splitter and a resistive TRIG star, and every module sits one equal cable from the root, so nothing builds up with N. The chain needs the fewest cables, 2(N − 1) short ones, but for eight modules the drift over seven hops uses most of the 50 ps budget. Both save the sync unit, 1U of rack and about 10 W. When a true SYSREF is wanted, load MASTER-TS or CHAIN-TS on the same cables, or use the sync unit.

Prefer a star, with a box or from a root module, when modules sit far apart, at 8 modules, when one module must be serviced while the others run, or when the skew target is below about 30 ps without re-calibration. The chain fits when N ≤ 4 and the fewest cables matter. Use the card-only chain on the lab bench.

12 V: a star, never a chain

Each module draws 4.58 A at 12 V. Chained through eight modules the first link would carry 36.6 A, and with 0.3 m links of 12 AWG the last module would see about 1.17 V less (contacts to measure). Feed every J30 from a distribution bar or a bus bar on the base plate: 1 m of 16 AWG drops only 0.12 V.

Ethernet

Keep the external switch with N + 1 ports: a dead module never cuts the others off, and it carries the profiles to every module. The on-carrier switch option (E2) is dropped so every carrier stays one build. The two RS-485 ports on each card can carry a slow backup link along the chain.

Open questions to check on hardware

  • Continuity on a delivered card: J66 → J67 pin 3 → CLKin0, J35 → R345 → CLKin1, R344 and R348 fitted, R699 on LMK_SYNC, K19 = PS_MIO26, R340 as card U48's only supply.
  • Nested zero-delay with the SYSREF divider as feedback (DZ) and with DCLKout8 (TS5) at a 5 MHz PFD on the card's PLL1 loop filter: lock, stability, settle time. Simulate in PLLatinum Sim first.
  • Phase repeatability over at least 20 power cycles (BENCH-DZ): card PL_CLK and PL_SYSREF against the 5 MHz edge, and the GTY clock from card J32 at 250 MHz.
  • TS5: exactly one gated SYNC edge (MON_SYNC = 1), PLL1 stays locked through the pin sync, and the VCO-edge margin per module.
  • LMK00804B: input network from 0.25 to 1.3 Vpp, idle-low, propagation delay and drift α per hop, part-to-part offset.
  • J32 through a DC block: amplitude and slew at J66 (card-only chain) and at carrier J45 into U27 in differential mode.
  • MTS latency reports across power cycles in a chain, and whether a forced capture slip shows up in them.
  • Whether the HamGeek boot firmware programs U46, and whether our firmware can own its SPI completely.
  • Splitter edge rate at 5 MHz and port-to-port delay match of ZFSC-4-1 and ZSC-2-1+; the edge rate at card J66.
  • TRIG IO through card J64 in both directions: a resistive star into 4 inputs and the active fan-out into 8, DC level and ringing at each A10, and the arrival spread.

The hop cables run between neighbouring rear panels: 250 mm on the bench and about 450 mm between rack shelves (estimate). In a master star the splitter and the TRIG star sit behind the modules, and every cable to them has the same length. Mechanics shows the panels; Sync & timing has the full profile table.

Step 6

GPIO map

The card's J65 header carries everything the carrier needs: an I²C bus, an SPI chain for the attenuators, and a few status and enable lines. The FPGA pins come from XCZU67DR-2FFVE1156I.ucf; all ten IOs sit in a 3.3 V HD bank. Header pin numbers still need checking against the PDF drawing. The trigger does not use J65: TRIG IO reaches FPGA pin A10 over coax through card J64. The three spare IOs now serve the carrier clock zone: IO3 is SYNC_GATE (out), IO8 MON_SYNC and IO9 MON_CLK (in), routed next to the ribbon GND pins 19/20.

Multi-board signals

Only the trigger is timing-critical between modules. It travels on coax into every card's J64: from the sync unit, from the TRIG master's J28 through a resistive star (N ≤ 4), an active fan-out in the kit (N > 4), or along a short bus in a chain. Everything else between modules (profiles, ready flags, latency reports, the common target latency) goes over Ethernet through the PC, where a few milliseconds don't matter.

The PL samples TRIG with the 250 MHz fabric clock (MMCM × 2 from the 125 MHz PL_CLK) and arms only on 4 consecutive high samples, so ringing on the 480 mm W25 stub cannot arm twice. The TRIG master drives 100 ns after its SYSREF edge, so a 200 ns SYSREF period leaves a wide margin. DC level at A10 (VIH 2.0 V): ≈ 2.4 V with a resistive star at 4 modules, ≈ 1.9–2.2 V at 8 (estimate), hence the fan-out or the GNSS-armed start above 4.

Timing · Clocks & power

Clocks and power budget

Every clock in a module comes from one 5 MHz CLK on CLK IN (J26): from the root module's J29 through a splitter or a chain, from a lab generator, or 5 / 10 MHz from a sync unit. On the bench the module's own Y1 TCXO ÷ 2 (LOCAL5) feeds it with no cable. The plan works when each rate divides cleanly into the next, so one pulse period is a whole number of bits, fabric words and DAC samples. The power budget sizes the 12 V supply for the whole array.

Clock-plan rules (PG269)

  • The DAC AXI4-Stream clock comes from PL_CLK through an MMCM, never from clk_dacX (p.188, p.190).
  • PL_CLK 125 MHz × 5 = 625 MHz is an integer ratio, but p.224 and p.359 say "common integer multiple" and every AMD example is a power of two: Vivado check before any board work.
  • Fabric clocks stay at or below 500 MHz; the 625 MHz DAC AXI domain is the one exception, so check its timing closure on the −2 part.
  • SYSREF stays below 10 MHz and a whole sub-multiple of every clock that samples it (p.187–188).
  • Fallbacks if Vivado says no: VCO0 2500 MHz with PL_CLK 625 MHz (÷ 4; DAC_REFCLK ÷ 5, GTY ÷ 10, SYSREF ÷ 500), or 8 GS/s with PL_CLK and AXI at 500 MHz. The checker presets show both.

    Build · Mechanics

    Mechanical concept

    The carrier lies flat in a small aluminium box and the HamGeek card stands upright in its slot, like a card in a PC, with its heatsink and fan facing the RF strips. The card's column of 19 SSMC connectors faces the front, about 31 mm behind the panel: room for the connector barrels, right-angle SSMC plugs and the bend of the 8 DAC jumpers back to the strips. Its I/O edge (Ethernet, DisplayPort, USB, both QSFP cages) lines up with a cut-out in the rear panel. The front panel carries the 16 RF outputs, so the cables to the DUT stay short and tidy, and in front of the card a removable inlet plate with the air slots. The plate carries no connectors: unscrew its four thumb screws and lift it off for direct access to the card's SSMC column (ADC inputs, GNSS, CLK0_IN). The rear panel takes the 12 V jack, Ethernet and the other card I/O, and four SMAs: CLK IN, SYSREF IN, TRIG IO and CLK/SYSREF OUT. TRIG IO is cabled straight to card J64, a direct FPGA pin, so the FPGA sets its direction. Every module is built the same way and nothing inside the box moves between sync options: the rear cable set and a software profile pick the option (see Sync & timing). Inside, the 8 one-bit strips sit next to the slot, so the GTY lanes stay short; the 8 DAC jumpers loop back along the card and cross over them to the RF-DAC strips on the far side. Carrier J32 (CLK) feeds card J66 (CLK0_IN), carrier J33 (SYSREF) feeds card J35, and card J32 (SYS_CLK_OUT) comes back to carrier J45 as the GTY reference. Air enters at the front and leaves through a rear fan, passing the card's heatsink on the way.

    The card size now comes from the vendor photos: about 235 × 148 mm (±3 %), measured against the x8 edge fingers, the QSFP cages and the RJ45. The other dimensions are estimates. Card J35 has no visible connector in the vendor photos. The one-time card prep, the same on every card, fits an SMA there and makes the SYSREF mod: remove R345 and R699, run a fixed-length coax from the J35-side pad of R345 to the LMK-side pad of R699, solder J67 on 2-3 and remove R340 so the card TCXO U48 is off. Carrier J32 then sends the 5 MHz CLK to J66 and carrier J33 drives the LMK SYNC pin through J35 in every profile; with derived SYSREF, U22 holds that pin low. Remove the card's four corner standoffs before fitting it: there is only about 9 mm to the side wall. Measure the card when it arrives and rescale.

The SMA flanges don't fit at the 7 mm strip pitch, so they sit on the panel. Each cable rises straight out of its plug, steps back to its own layer (one-bit cables in front, RF-DAC cables 11 mm behind), crosses over and runs straight into the SMA plug: bends of 5 mm radius or more, at least 0.3 mm between any two cables at every card length.
    2. TRIG IO (J28) has no carrier part: W25 (≈ 480 mm) runs over the card's top edge straight to card J64 (PPS_IN, 33 Ω to FPGA pin A10), and the FPGA sets the direction. From the clock zone two jumpers run over the card's top edge: W21 from J32 (U20, CLK) to card J66 (CLK0_IN, J67 soldered on 2-3, LMK CLKin0), AC-coupled by the series 0.1 µF on the carrier, and W22 from J33 (U22, DC-coupled SYNC driver) to card J35, the LMK SYNC pin after the R699 mod. Card J32 (SYS_CLK_OUT, 250 MHz) returns to carrier J45 (GTY REF IN) over W23; C20 on the carrier blocks its DC. W21, W22, W23 and W25 stay plugged in every sync option.
    3. Rear exhaust fan and the 12 V input jack J30, labelled "12V 6A".
    4. Cut-out in the rear panel for the card's I/O edge: RJ45 (Ethernet), DisplayPort, USB 3.0, QSFP1 and QSFP2, plus the micro-USB and the power switch.
    5. Removable inlet plate: a 2 mm plate on four captive thumb screws (press-in nuts in the front panel) over the opening in front of the card, with 18 air slots (≈ 1900 mm²) and a dust filter. It carries no connectors or cables. Unscrew it for direct access to the card's SSMC column: the ADC inputs and J57 (GNSS antenna); J66 and J64 carry W21 and W25.

    Card J32 as a reference

    Card J32 (SYS_CLK_OUT) is the card's only external clock output: LMK04828 SDCLKOUT5, single-ended and DC-coupled LVPECL (about 0.4–0.6 Vpp into 50 Ω, estimate), so every cable from it needs an inline DC block. Its clock group shares only DCLKOUT4 (ADC_REFCLK1, an RF-ADC tile we do not use), so J32 is free to run at VCO/1…32 (250 MHz = ÷12 at VCO1 3000 MHz) or from the SYSREF divider (5 MHz = ÷600).

    UseVerdictHow
    GTY referenceYes, recommendedJ32 at 250 MHz (LVPECL 2000 mV format, check) → W23 (≈ 250 mm coax) → carrier J45 GTY REF IN → DC block → U27 (LMK1D1204 class in differential input mode: IN0_P terminated in 49.9 Ω, IN0_N AC-coupled to VAC_REF; it needs 0.3 Vpp and runs to 2 GHz, while its single-ended mode stops at 250 MHz) → PCIE_CLK edge pins (10 nF on the card) → quad A refclk1, shared with quad B. QPLL0 N = 40 gives 10 GHz and 20 Gb/s. The GTYs are then locked to the card's own PL_CLK, DAC and SYSREF clocks, and 250 MHz = 50 × 5 MHz gives one fixed phase to SYSREF. Release the GTY QPLL only after the card LMK has locked, synced and settled. Jitter ≈ 100 fs plus a few tens of fs from the buffer. W23 stays plugged in every profile; the carrier has no U21.
    Daisy-chain referenceBare-card chain A1 onlyOnly the bare-card chain A1 (bring-up, no carriers) uses it: SDCLKout5 from the SYSREF divider at 5 MHz through a DC block to the next card's J66 (derived SYSREF; a register setting, no rework). The GTY then runs from the free-running SI5341, so the one-bit rows are not locked to the DACs. With carriers J32 is the GTY reference in every profile: a chain relays the 5 MHz through carrier U28, and the legacy two-splitter cabling takes its SYSREF from the root's J29, not from card J32.

    Card J64 and J57 in our system

    Both sit in the card's front SSMC column (schematic p. 17). J64 is a direct FPGA I/O, so it becomes our TRIG IO without a board change. J57 feeds the on-card GNSS receiver, whose time pulse reaches only the FPGA, not the LMK.

    ConnectorVerdictHow
    J64 PPS_INYes, as TRIG IO, no tweakJ64 → R245 33 Ω → FPGA pin A10 (3.3 V HD bank), R248 1 kΩ pull-down, TPD4E001 ESD. As input: a direct LVCMOS33 trigger into the PL (1 kΩ load; drive it from a series-terminated source). As output: FPGA driver + 33 Ω ≈ a 50 Ω series-terminated source into coax. Do not add a 50 Ω shunt, it would load the driver. W25 (≈ 480 mm) from the rear TRIG IO; the carrier trigger receiver, the PERST# trigger route and J42 go away. Level budget (estimate): a resistive star gives ≈ 2.4 V at A10 for 4 modules against VIH 2.0 V; above 4 modules use an active TRIG fan-out or the GNSS-armed start, and arm on a qualified level.
    J57 GNSS antennaYes, for time of dayJ57 → NEO-M8N RF_IN, antenna bias from VCC_RF through L40 10 nH (active antenna). TIMEPULSE goes only to FPGA pin A9 (GNSS_PPS), tens-of-ns class (check the NEO-M8N datasheet): timestamps, or arming every module on the same GNSS second and starting on the first common SYSREF edge after it (PPS spread ≪ the 200 ns SYSREF period), so no trigger cable is needed when every module sees GNSS. Not a clock reference for ps alignment. There is no rear GNSS port: the antenna (or a GNSS splitter arm) reaches card J57 through the front SSMC access with the inlet plate off, or through a front-panel feed-through fitted by the user. Nothing on the card changes.

    Level budget at the LMK00804B inputs (estimate): J29 drives ≈ 1.65 Vpp into 50 Ω and the −3 dB input tap leaves 1.17 Vpp after a chain hop, ≈ 0.52 Vpp after a 1:4 splitter, ≈ 0.37 Vpp after 1:8 and ≈ 0.25 Vpp on the legacy 1:2 + 1:8 path (splitter loss 10·log10 N + 1 dB), inside the 0.25–1.3 Vpp input spec after the tap (LMK00804B VID 0.15–1.3 V, check); the legacy path sits at its lower edge, so measure it. Only square sources: the splitters must pass ≤ 1 MHz to ≥ 500 MHz so the 5 MHz edges stay fast, which rules out ZFSC-8-1 (0.5–175 MHz) and ZFSC-2-1 (5–500 MHz). TRIG must land inside one 200 ns SYSREF period; a resistive star gives ≈ 2.4 V at FPGA A10 for 4 modules against VIH 2.0 V, but only ≈ 1.9–2.2 V for 8, so above 4 modules use an active TRIG fan-out or the GNSS-armed start.

    What stays the same

    The carrier design, the card prep, the firmware image and the start-up sequence. Every module is identical, so any module can be the root, and a spare can replace any other after a skew re-calibration and a new MTS run.

    What changes

    The external sync kit: splitter size, TRIG star or active fan-out, and the cable count. With the sync unit and true SYSREF (UNIT-TS), 8 modules need 16 outputs (CLK + SYSREF) against the LMK04832's 14, so add buffers; UNIT-DZ needs 8. Supply size and rack space grow linearly.

    Mixing with the existing ZCU216

    The ZCU216's CLK104 can take CLK and SYSREF from the same sync unit, adding 16 DAC channels to the array. It needs its own front end (an RFMC mezzanine), and its outputs will differ slightly from the HamGeek channels, so calibrate it as a separate group.

    DAC-only modules

    If a module only needs RF-DAC outputs, leave the one-bit front ends unpopulated and skip the GTY rework. The 16-DAC option then costs two cards plus two lighter carriers.

    Roadmap

    Roadmap and open items

    Five phases take the design from one card on the bench to a calibrated array at the DUT. Each phase ends at a gate, and each open item belongs to the phase that has to close it.

    Sync bench milestones, in order

    The one-build sync design (Sync & timing) rests on these checks. Each one gates the next; the tag names the phase that runs it.

    1. Vivado 125 / 625 MHz check. RFdc IP in Advanced mode with 10 GS/s DUC bypass, 16 samples per word, MTS on and PL clock 125 MHz: the GUI and DRC accept it, 625 MHz closes timing on the −2 part, and the DS926 AXI4-Stream maximum allows it. If not, switch to VCO0 2500 MHz or 8 GS/s. P0
    2. LMK00804B input-network test. AC-coupled single-ended drive with the offset bias: clean switching from 0.25 to 1.3 Vpp at 5 and 10 MHz, no chatter at the 1:8 and legacy 1:2 + 1:8 levels, idle low with nothing connected, and the J26 stub shared by U20 and U28. P1
    3. BENCH-DZ repeatability. Lock, settle time and phase of PL_CLK, PL_SYSREF and the MTS latency repeat over 20+ power cycles with the dual-loop-first divider sync. Measure the dual-loop ambiguity (≥ 4 positions, ≈ 83 ps apart) once on the same card. P1
    4. TS5 single-edge check. The U61 gate passes exactly one SYNC edge (MON_SYNC count = 1), SYNC_DIS8 keeps PLL1 locked, every other divider resets, DCLKout8_HS lies inside the feedback path, and PL_SYSREF sits ≥ 1.5 ns from every PL_CLK edge. P1
    5. PLLatinum loop decision. PLL1 at a 5 MHz PFD with the 50 µA minimum charge pump on the HamGeek filter: keep it, or make one identical filter change on every card before the card prep is frozen. P1
    6. Splitter edge and delay match. Edge rate at 5 MHz, low-frequency corner and port-to-port delay match of the ZFSC-4-1 and ZSC-2-1+ (and a wide-band 8-way if used). The ZSC-2-1+ stops at 400 MHz, below the ≥ 500 MHz band rule, so its 5 MHz edge decides whether it stays in the N = 8 cascade and the legacy cabling. P2
    7. TRIG level budget. DC high and ringing at FPGA A10 for the chosen N: resistive star ≈ 2.4 V at 4 modules (estimate) against VIH 2.0 V, level-qualified arming; above 4 modules an active fan-out or the GNSS-armed start. P2
    8. Multi-module MASTER-DZ. Two, then four modules on one splitter: MTS target from ≥ 5 power cycles per module, skew repeats; MASTER-TS on the same cables as the A/B check. P2
    1. P0

      Evaluate one card

      2–4 weeks

      Goal. Prove that one HamGeek card does what the design assumes before we draw the carrier.

      Tasks

      • Run the Vivado check first: RFdc IP with PL_CLK 125 MHz and a 625 MHz DAC AXI4-Stream clock from one MMCM (milestone 1).
      • Bring up one HamGeek card: power, JTAG, PCIe and the RF-DAC tiles.
      • Lock the LMK04828 PLL1 to an external 5 MHz CLK on J66 (CLKin0, J67 on 2-3).
      • Test card J64 as TRIG IO in both directions: drive FPGA pin A10 into 50 Ω coax and check the edge, then take a series-terminated trigger in and check the A10 threshold.
      • Optional: fit an active antenna on J57, read GNSS time and check the PPS on FPGA pin A9.
      • Do the one-time card prep on one card (checklist: fixed-length J35 → SYNC coax, J67 link, R340 out, MIO settings) and check MTS repeatability over power cycles with derived SYSREF and with one gated SYSREF edge on J35.
      • Program J32 to 250 MHz and lock the GTY QPLL from it through the carrier buffer; confirm the GTY-to-SYSREF phase repeats over power cycles.
      • Run GTY TX0–3 at 20 Gb/s raw (QPLL0 N = 40) from that 250 MHz refclk on the PCIE_CLK pins.
      • Do the TX4–7 rework (fit C632–35 and C1022–25, remove the QSFP2 0 Ω parts) and repeat the 20 Gb/s test.
      • Measure the card DAC path (0.1 µF, TCM2-63WX+, SSMC) from 100 kHz to 6 GHz.
      • Decide between the UWB2-50E balun swap and the single-ended bypass.

      Open items

      Exit gate. Vivado accepts the clock plan (or a fallback is chosen). Eight GTY lanes run at 20 Gb/s, the DAC path is measured, and the balun choice is written down. PLL1 locks to CLK on J66, J64 works as TRIG IO both ways, and on the prepped card the MTS latency repeats over power cycles with derived SYSREF and with SYSREF on J35.

      Stages Card findings Module Sync & timing Clocks & power
    2. P1

      Carrier prototype

      One module

      Goal. Turn one card into a working module: 3 V outputs into 50 Ω with a DC level on every channel, and the bench sync profiles proven.

      Tasks

      • Draw the carrier schematic and layout: slot J1, SSMC inputs J2–J9, AFE, PA, power and the clock zone (U20, U22, U28 LMK00804B, Y1 + U29, U30 TCA9538, U59–U61).
      • Test the J26 / J27 input network on a test board or the first carrier before the layout is frozen (milestone 2).
      • Run BENCH-DZ and BENCH-TS on one module with no sync cables (milestones 3–5).
      • Build both DAC path variants: the UWB2-50E transformer (T1) and the single-ended option (R1/R2).
      • Test the staged chokes (L1, L2, L5) and gain blocks (U1, U2) at low frequency on a test board.
      • Reach 3 V into 50 Ω on all 8 DAC and 8 one-bit outputs.
      • Bring up the DC-level stage: U31/U32 AD5675R and the U33–U40 buffers.

      Open items

      Exit gate. One module drives 3 V pulses into 50 Ω on every output over the agreed frequency range, with the DC level set per output. BENCH-DZ repeats over 20+ power cycles and BENCH-TS passes exactly one SYNC edge.

      Stages Carrier schematic Signal fidelity GPIO Sync & timing Clocks & power
    3. P2

      Two-module sync

      Two modules

      Goal. Show that two modules sharing one CLK and one TRIG put their pulses out at a known, repeatable skew.

      Tasks

      • Set up MASTER-DZ: software makes one module the root (Y1 and LOCAL5 on, U28 → J29); J29 into a ZFSC-4-1, equal cables to both CLK IN, the root's loop-back included.
      • Measure the splitters: edge rate at 5 MHz, port-to-port delay match, and the level after the −3 dB tap (1:2 ≈ 0.78 Vpp, 1:4 ≈ 0.52 Vpp, 1:8 ≈ 0.37 Vpp, estimate); check that U20 switches cleanly (milestone 6).
      • Run MTS across two cards with derived SYSREF; set the common target from ≥ 5 power cycles per module; then run MASTER-TS on the same cables as the A/B check (milestone 8).
      • Drive TRIG IO from the root through a resistive star into both J64 inputs, measure the DC high and ringing at A10 (milestone 7), and check that every power-up starts on the same fabric cycle.
      • Run cable discovery and check that the profile checker refuses a mis-patch (two roots, a missing loop-back, a leaf driving J29) and names the connector.
      • Measure output-to-output skew between the two modules and settle the calibration method.
      • Optional: GNSS-armed start. Arm both modules on the same GNSS second (antenna on card J57 through the front SSMC access, PPS on A9) and check that they start on the same SYSREF edge without a TRIG cable.

      Open items

      Exit gate. The skew between two modules repeats across power cycles in MASTER-DZ, MASTER-TS agrees with it, and the chosen calibration method removes it.

      Stages Sync & timing Scaling
    4. P3

      Four-module array

      Four modules

      Goal. Scale to the full array of 32 DAC columns and 32 one-bit rows.

      Tasks

      • Build four identical carriers from the P1 design with the P2 fixes folded in, and prep four cards the same way.
      • Pick bench or rack mechanics and mount the cards, carriers, the clock source, the switch and the MS-A2 control PC.
      • Size and wire the 12 V supply for the whole array.
      • Cable the chosen sync profile (CLK, SYSREF if used, TRIG IO) with one equal-length cable set, and GbE from each module and the PC to the switch. Re-sync and re-run MTS after any re-cable.

      Open items

      Exit gate. All 64 outputs play one pattern, in step, under control from the PC.

      Stages Mechanics Scaling Carrier parts Clocks & power
    5. P4

      Calibration and DUT integration

      Full array

      Goal. Turn the array into an instrument the experiment can drive.

      Tasks

      • Measure and store a skew table for every channel, keyed by profile, cable set and card + carrier serial.
      • Measure and store an amplitude table for every channel.
      • Measure warm-up drift and set how long the array warms up before calibration.
      • Define the software API on the PC: load patterns, set DC levels, pick a sync profile, arm and trigger.
      • Connect the DUT and run the first pulse sequence.

      Open items

      No open items yet.

      Exit gate. The DUT sees calibrated pulses on every channel from one software call.

      Stages Sync & timing Overview

    That closes the loop from requirements to a working array. To see how each phase fits the signal chain again, go back to the Overview.
